definition: Mountain Car, a standard testing domain in Reinforcement learning, is a problem in which an under-powered car must drive up a steep hill.
details: Since gravity is stronger than the car's engine, even at full throttle, the car cannot simply accelerate up the steep slope. The car is situated in a valley and must learn to leverage potential energy by driving up the opposite hill before the car is able to make it to the goal at the top of the rightmost hill. The domain has been used as a test bed in various reinforcement learning papers.

explainer.lead: Mountain Car is a standard reinforcement-learning test domain where a weak car must reach a hilltop it cannot climb by direct acceleration. It matters because it forces an agent to learn indirect, non-greedy strategies.

tiers.eli5: You are in a valley in a toy car whose engine is too weak to climb the hill, so you have to roll backwards up the other slope first to build enough momentum to make it over.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to sanity-check exploration and credit assignment in RL algorithms; the pitfall is that greedy or purely reward-seeking policies fail, so the agent must learn to move away from the goal first.
tiers.paperLevel: The domain is a valley with an under-powered car: gravity is stronger than the engine even at full throttle, so the car must drive up the opposite hill to leverage potential energy before reaching the goal at the top of the rightmost hill.

explainer.example: An agent that always accelerates toward the goal stalls on the slope; one that first drives up the left hill stores enough potential energy to reach the right-hand goal.
